items.title: Spending: from goods to services and loans
items.text: Trade-in funds ¥50bn lower, services retail +4.9% in Jan–Aug

items.title: Equipment: funds and cheaper loans
items.text: ¥200bn allocated, and firm loans get a 1.5 pt subsidy

items.title: Carbon: a new yearly yardstick
items.text: Carbon intensity down about 3.8% this year, 17% over five years

items.title: Exports: still the bright spot
items.text: Exports +13.4% in H1, goods trade +17.6% in Jan–Aug

footnote: Source: 2026 Government Work Report, NBS and Ministry of Finance releases (July–September 2026)
notes: What the four lines mean for us. Spending: central support is shifting from goods trade-ins toward services and loan subsidies. Trade-in money is ¥50 billion lower than last year, and services are growing faster than retail sales, so our consumer business should look harder at services and financing offers. Equipment: ¥200 billion for equipment upgrades is out, small firms get a 1.5-point loan subsidy on up to ¥75 million, and the AI Plus manufacturing plan is under way, so upgrade projects have both funding and cheaper credit. Carbon: the yearly target is now carbon intensity, down 17% over five years, and the Plan calls for zero-carbon factories and parks, so energy-heavy plants should get their carbon accounts in order first. Exports: exports grew 13.4% in the first half, the strongest part of demand this year, and are worth protecting.
